{{Quote|Dradan, Dradan.|Dreambeast Dradan, upon meeting Rebel Alliance operatives on Trinta|<ref name="Domain of Evil">''[[Domain of Evil]]''</ref>}}
The '''Dradan''' were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of peaceful [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] native to a [[Unidentified Dradan homeworld|planet]] in the [[Drada system/Legends|Drada system]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. After the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] was [[New Order/Legends|formed]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] and began to [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|hunt]] and [[Death/Legends|kill]] the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], the Dradan offered their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] as a refuge to [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] fugitives. The Empire discovered the Dradan's treachery by [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]] and retaliated with [[Speciecide|genocide]] of the species and despoliation of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].

When the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|fallen Jedi]] [[Halagad Ventor]] fled [[Torture/Legends|torture]] at the hands of the Empire and took up a hermit's existence on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Trinta]], he tapped into the world's natural [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] [[Vergence/Legends|Force nexus]] to create [[Mind trick/Legends|illusions]] known as [[dreambeast]]s to chase away anyone who visited the swampy planet. Among the apparitions he used for those purposes were Dradan, whom Ventor presented as thin [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] with [[Color/Legends|red]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and simple technology. When a group of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[operative]]s landed on Trinta, Ventor sent his spectral Dradan to lure them into eating [[Poison/Legends|poisonous]] food. However, Ventor's control over the illusions was incomplete, and the Rebels rejected the false Dradan's offering. Upon his failure, Ventor dissipated the phantasms.

==Biology and appearance==
The Dradan were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. In an [[Mind trick/Legends|illusion]] created to misdirect outsiders who visited the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Trinta]], the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Halagad Ventor]] presented them as tall [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] with thin frames and five-fingered [[Limb/Legends|hands]]. Each of Ventor's illusions had large [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] that glowed [[Color/Legends|red]]; a wide mouth; a flat, broad nose; two [[Human/Legends|Human]]-like [[Ear/Legends|ears]]; and a head of long [[Hair/Legends|hair]]. As long as he concentrated on his illusion, Ventor's Dradan had calm and peaceable expressions. However, when his attention was distracted, the illusory humanoids instead exhibited menacing grimaces; savage-looking eyes; prominent, sharp [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]]; and long claws.<ref name="CAV2" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|S'jak, S'jak!|Dreamscape Dradan, attempting to convince Rebel operatives to follow them|<ref name="CAV2" />}}
The Dradan were a peaceful people. In the apparitions presented by Halagad Ventor, they dressed in plain, white robes and carried simple, [[Wood/Legends|wooden]] implements. They cooked meat over a fire and served it on wooden plates, accompanied by [[Fruit/Legends|fruit]] and [[Vegetable/Legends|vegetables]]. Ventor's Dradan spoke a [[Dradan language|simple language]] and used mime and gesture to communicate with those who did not understand them. The illusory Dradan were skittish and fled at any sign of hostility.<ref name="CAV2" />

==History==
The Dradan species hailed from a [[Unidentified Dradan homeworld|world]]<ref name="CAV2" /> in the [[Drada system/Legends|Drada system]],<ref name="Atlas" /><ref name="Planetnamia" /> a [[Star system/Legends|star system]] that became integrated into the [[The galaxy/Legends|greater galaxy]] at some point between [[3000 BBY|3000]] and [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]].<ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> The world eventually fell within the bounds of the [[Halthor sector/Legends|Halthor sector]]<ref name="Atlas" /> in the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]] region of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. From [[1004 BBY|1004]] to [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], as the [[New Sith Wars]] raged, the system fell within unaligned or contested [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. By [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the system was within space allied to the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="EA" />

As the Republic [[New Order/Legends|gave way]] to a successor state, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], in 19 BBY, [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] declared [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]]&mdash;a command that resulted in the systematic [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] of the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] and led to the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], whereby all remaining [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were hunted down and [[Death/Legends|killed]].<ref name="NEC 84">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> In response, the Dradan offered their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] as a safe haven to Jedi fleeing persecution. However, when the Empire discovered the Dradan's pro-Jedi policy, they retaliated by [[Speciecide|exterminating]] the entire species and scorching their planet. Nothing but cinders remained<ref name="CAV2" /> by [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]].<ref name="date">Based on the appearance of Rebel Alliance agents in ''Domain of Evil'', the adventure must occur after the formation of the Alliance, which happened in 2 BBY, as established in ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''. In ''The Dark Forces Saga, Part 2'', it is mentioned that Qu Rahn heard a report of the death of Halagad Ventor&mdash;who dies during the events of ''Domain of Evil''&mdash;before he contacted [[Morgan Katarn]]. This implies that Ventor died before Morgan Katarn, whose own death occurred in 1 BBY, per ''[[Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire]]''.</ref>

==Dradan in the galaxy==
At some point after the Clone Wars, a fallen Jedi Knight named Halagad Ventor fled to the planet Trinta to escape the notice of the Empire. The world had a strong [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] [[Vergence/Legends|nexus]], upon which Ventor drew to create powerful [[The Force/Legends|Force]] illusions known as [[dreambeast]]s. The phantasms reflected Ventor's fears and inner turmoil born of his experiences of [[Torture/Legends|torture]] at the hands of the Empire, and he used them to mask his presence on the world and to drive away intruders. Among his repertoire of illusions was a group of simple Dradan swamp dwellers.<ref name="CAV2" />

At some point between [[2 BBY/Legends|2]] and 1 BBY,<ref name="date" /> a group of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[operative]]s fled to Trinta, followed by their pursuers, a [[Taloron]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] named [[Crutag]] and his crew.<ref name="CAV2" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1}}
[[File:HalagadVentor-Interrogation.jpg|thumb|left|After his torture by the Empire, Halagad Ventor fled to Trinta, where he presented dreambeasts to scare off any intruders.]]
In an effort to draw the intruders away from their [[Starship/Legends|starship]] and harm them, Ventor created illusions of about twenty-five Dradan and brought them from the swamps to introduce themselves to the Rebels. The Dradan dreambeasts gestured for the strangers to follow them and led them to a campsite. Because Ventor directed the apparitions' actions from afar, his illusions were far from perfect; for instance, his Dradan sometimes walked through [[Tree/Legends|trees]] and other solid objects. Similarly, Ventor concentrated on the appearance and actions of the Dradan within the Rebels' line of sight, so that those walking behind the offworlders grew translucent and fuzzy, and their features eventually grew savage and evil-looking.<ref name="CAV2" />

Nevertheless, the Rebels followed Ventor's Dradan illusions to a campsite in a clearing, where a carcass lay over an open fire and fruit and vegetables awaited consumption.Unbeknownst to the Rebels, however, the food was also illusory and masked [[Poison/Legends|poisonous]] substances. As the Dradan figures beckoned the offworlders to eat, the phantoms' appearance shifted from friendly and welcoming to menacing and evil. The Rebels chose not to partake in the feast, and Ventor dissipated the incorporeal figures.<ref name="CAV2" />
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
The Dradan are mentioned ''[[Domain of Evil]]'', an [[adventure]] written by [[Jim Bambra]] and published by [[West End Games]] in [[1991]] as part of their ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' line. The story takes place after the Dradan species has been wiped out by the Empire, so only Ventor's false Dradan make an appearance. The adventure fails to indicate whether Ventor's illusions reflect actual Dradan biology, culture, and society, or simply the fallen Jedi's fevered imagination. An illustration of the dreambeast Dradan, drawn by artist [[Allen Nunis]], accompanies the adventure.<ref name="CAV2" /> Author [[Eric S. Trautmann]] revised ''Domain of Evil'' for ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition]]'', as part of the [[1995]] sourcebook ''[[Classic Adventures: Volume Two]]''. Trautmann's update retains most of Bambra's details about the species with one exception: a line spoken by Ventor's illusions as they beckon for the player characters to follow them into the forest changes from "Sajak, Sajak!" to "S'jak, S'jak!"<ref name="CAV2" />

This article assumes that the player characters follow Ventor's Dradan illusions to their camp but reject the food the Dradan offer. However, the adventure also allows the characters to ignore the Dradan completely or attack the apparitions, in which case the figures dissipate. Partaking of the food offered by the Dradan dreambeasts poisons and possibly kills any character who consumes it.<ref name="CAV2" />
